scenes.text: Hay-fever patients miss the season start. PollenPlan asked whether a simple alert rule beats the forecast itself — on real pollen counts.

This is the live demo. Madrid, Basel, Zurich. Olive, grass, birch. Twenty-eight seasons in the onset table — including the seasons every rule missed. Every number on this page comes from one pre-registered backtest.

Eighty-six tests, green. Six rules, frozen before the run: persistence, API persistence, the API's own forecast, our two-day rule, the pre-peak alert, and climatology. Madrid olive: thirteen point six percent. Grass: thirty-one point four. Below our own bar — flagged as limits, not hidden.

The verdict. The API's own forecast caught forty-one point six percent of high days — eight hundred sixty-three events, eight thousand seventy-six city-days. Our rule caught forty-one. It did not beat the API. So the headline is the measured skill.

What it doesn't show. The early alert fires three days sooner — by construction: it reads three days of forecast, and archived values may flatter it live. Thresholds are published-panel values, signed off. Retrospective. Not a medical device.
Measured skill, open code, open data. Try the demo now — no account.

voice_name: Daniel (ElevenLabs premade, neutral broadcaster; not an imitation of the author)
